domain_label: Ingredient Ratios & Crumb Structure (Recipe Formulation & Baking Chemistry subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark bake evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in baking-science principles
exclusions: frosting and filling formulation internals, decoration, packaging, and industrial depositing equipment

competency_questions.question: How is each ingredient expressed as a baker's percentage of flour?
How does a percentage formula scale to a target yield without ratio drift?
What high-ratio rule keeps cupcake batter a stable emulsion?
How much liquid is needed relative to flour and sugar?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HYDRATION sets flour:liquid and sugar dissolution

competency_questions.question: Which ingredients build structure versus tenderize the crumb?
How is a target crumb evaluated and tied back to ratio levers?
How does mixing method control gluten development?
How do leavening and bake conditions set rise and dome?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAVENING and DOME_RISE define rise control

competency_questions.question: What structural and emulsifying roles does egg play, and what safety does it impose?
How does sugar tenderize, retain moisture, and balance against flavor?
How do sugar, fat, and liquid combine to set moistness and shelf-life?
How does fat type and quantity affect tenderness, flavor, and mouthfeel?
How does total hydration affect crumb moisture and batter viscosity?
How is the soda:acid balance set for lift and browning?

glossary.definition: each ingredient weight expressed as a percentage of total flour weight
cake formula where sugar weight equals or exceeds flour weight, requiring high-ratio flour and enough liquid
ingredient that strengthens crumb via protein or starch network, mainly flour and egg
ingredient that weakens or shortens structure, mainly sugar, fat, and leavening
ratio of total liquid to flour controlling batter consistency and crumb moisture
stable dispersion of fat in the water phase that high-ratio batter depends on
able to attract and hold water, the property by which sugar retains crumb moisture
firming and drying of crumb over time from starch retrogradation and moisture loss
internal cell structure and texture of the baked cupcake

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cupcake ingredient-ratio and crumb-structure work units in absence of supplied bake datasets, grounded in established baking-science principles
grounding_limits: not derived from measured bake data

nodes.definition: Express every cupcake ingredient as a percentage of total flour weight so a formula can be scaled, compared, and rebalanced predictably.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Anchors all balance decisions to one reproducible reference base
pros.example: fat at 50% of flour reads the same across batch sizes

cons.claim: Wrong base weight silently distorts every downstream ratio
cons.example: counting cocoa as flour skews hydration

acceptance_tests: every ingredient expressed relative to flour=100%
formula scales to 2x without ratio drift
revisit_triggers: new ingredient class added to formula
switch between cake and high-ratio flour

nodes.definition: Enforce the high-ratio rule that sugar weight >= flour weight and liquid weight >= sugar weight so the batter stays a stable pourable emulsion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Keeps tender, fine-crumb cupcakes that hold moisture without collapse
pros.example: sugar 110% of flour gives velvety crumb

cons.claim: Breaking the emulsion window curdles batter and produces greasy or sunken cupcakes
cons.example: liquid below sugar weight breaks the batter

failure_modes: ordinary flour cannot carry high sugar
revisit_triggers: sugar load pushed beyond emulsion limit

nodes.definition: Classify each ingredient as a structure-builder (flour protein, egg) or tenderizer (sugar, fat, leavening) and tune their balance to hit a target crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Lets a baker move one lever knowing how crumb shifts before baking
pros.example: cut flour, add sugar to soften a dry crumb

cons.claim: Adjusting one lever blind to its class over-tenderizes and collapses the crumb
cons.example: more fat and sugar with no structure offset sinks cupcakes

acceptance_tests: each ingredient labeled toughener or tenderizer
net structure change predicted before bake
revisit_triggers: repeated collapse traced to lever imbalance

nodes.definition: Select flour by protein content (cake vs all-purpose vs high-ratio) to set gluten potential and target crumb fineness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Low-protein cake flour yields a fine, tender crumb that carries high sugar
pros.example: 8% protein cake flour for velvety cupcakes

cons.claim: High-protein flour over-develops gluten and toughens the cupcake
cons.example: bread flour makes chewy, tunneled crumb

failure_modes: using bread flour for tender cake
acceptance_tests: flour protein matched to target crumb
gluten potential consistent with sugar load

nodes.definition: Choose mixing method (high-ratio two-stage, creaming, or blending) to control gluten development and air incorporation for the target crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Two-stage method coats flour in fat first, limiting gluten for a tender crumb
pros.example: high-ratio method gives fine even cupcakes

cons.claim: Overmixing develops gluten and produces tunnels and toughness
cons.example: long mix after flour toughens batter

acceptance_tests: mix method matched to fat state and flour

nodes.definition: Set egg quantity and form (whole vs separated, whites vs yolks) to add protein structure, lift, and lecithin emulsification.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Yolk lecithin stabilizes the high-ratio emulsion while white protein sets structure
pros.example: whole eggs give lift plus moisture binding

cons.claim: Too much egg dries and toughens; too little fails to set the crumb
cons.example: excess whites make rubbery dry cupcakes

failure_modes: too little egg to set structure
acceptance_tests: egg ratio supports both structure and emulsion
no rubbery or collapsed crumb in trial
revisit_triggers: emulsion instability traced to low yolk

nodes.definition: Tune sugar load and type to tenderize by interfering with gluten and starch, retain moisture hygroscopically, and drive browning and flavor.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Sugar tenderizes, holds moisture, and extends softness over days
pros.example: high sugar keeps cupcakes moist on day three

cons.claim: Cutting sugar for less sweetness also removes moisture, tenderness, and browning
cons.example: low-sugar cupcakes go dry and pale

failure_modes: cutting sugar without offsetting moisture loss
acceptance_tests: sugar load matched to sweetness and shelf-life target
crumb stays tender and moist as planned
revisit_triggers: sugar load reduced for diet target

nodes.definition: Choose fat type (butter, oil, shortening) and quantity to coat flour proteins for tenderness, carry flavor, and set mouthfeel and moistness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Oil stays liquid for a moister crumb; butter trades some moisture for flavor
pros.example: oil cupcakes read moister than butter at equal weight

cons.claim: Too much fat over-tenderizes and greases; too little gives a dry, tough crumb

failure_modes: choosing flavor fat where moistness is the goal
acceptance_tests: fat type matched to flavor vs moistness goal
revisit_triggers: flavor target shifts toward butter richness

nodes.definition: Set total liquid relative to flour to fully hydrate flour and dissolve sugar, controlling batter viscosity, spread, and crumb moisture.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Adequate liquid dissolves sugar and hydrates flour for an even, moist crumb
pros.example: milk at 100% of flour gives pourable high-ratio batter

cons.claim: Too little liquid leaves grainy undissolved sugar and a dry, dense crumb
cons.example: low hydration yields tough domed cupcakes

acceptance_tests: liquid sufficient to dissolve sugar and hydrate flour

nodes.definition: Balance baking powder and soda quantity and soda:acid ratio to set rise, cell size, doming, and pH-driven crumb color and browning.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Correct leavening gives even rise and tender open crumb
pros.example: 1.25% baking powder lifts without coarse holes

cons.claim: Excess leavening over-expands then collapses and coarsens the crumb
cons.example: too much soda gives soapy taste and sunken tops

acceptance_tests: leavener dose matched to rise target

nodes.definition: Control oven spring and doming via leavening, flour structure, oven temperature, and fill level to get the intended cupcake top shape.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Tuned temp and leavening give the chosen rounded or flat top
pros.example: hotter start sets a higher dome

cons.claim: Wrong heat or fill cracks, peaks, or sinks the top

failure_modes: temperature too low to set rise
acceptance_tests: no cracking or sinking in trial bake
revisit_triggers: doming target changes for frosting style

nodes.definition: Manage staling by balancing sugar, fat, liquid, and invert sugars to keep cupcakes moist over their intended shelf-life.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Higher sugar and oil keep crumb soft for days

cons.claim: Optimizing only fresh texture leaves cupcakes stale by day two

failure_modes: trading shelf-life for fresh-only texture blindly

nodes.definition: Define and apply objective crumb evaluation (cell size, uniformity, moistness, tenderness, height) to judge whether a formula hit its target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: A rubric ties each crumb defect back to a ratio lever for repair
pros.example: tunnels point to overmixing or excess leavening

cons.claim: Judging by taste alone hides structural defects until scaled up
cons.example: moist but tunneled crumb passes a taste-only check

acceptance_tests: each defect mapped to a causal lever
revisit_triggers: recurrent defect not explained by rubric

nodes.definition: Balance total sweetness against flavor complexity (salt, acid, cocoa, vanilla, browning) so the cupcake reads delicious, not merely sweet.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Salt and acid cut sweetness and reveal complexity at the same sugar level
pros.example: a pinch of salt makes vanilla read deeper

cons.claim: Chasing more sugar flattens flavor into one-note sweetness

failure_modes: adding sugar where flavor contrast is needed
acceptance_tests: flavor reads complex not flat in tasting

nodes.definition: Coordinate cupcake sweetness with the planned frosting so the assembled product is balanced, lowering cake sugar when frosting is very sweet.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Slightly less-sweet cake balances a sweet buttercream into a harmonious whole

cons.claim: Optimizing cake sweetness in isolation makes the assembled cupcake cloying
cons.example: sweet cake plus sweet frosting overwhelms

failure_modes: ignoring frosting sugar in the budget
acceptance_tests: cake and frosting balance in tasting

nodes.definition: Enforce food-safety limits (no raw egg/dairy hazards, temperature danger zone, full bake-through, allergen control) that override any flavor or texture choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Guarantees the cupcake is safe to eat regardless of texture goals
pros.example: fully baked center kills egg pathogens

cons.claim: Underbaking for a moister center can leave unsafe raw egg

acceptance_tests: no raw-egg hazard in final product

nodes.definition: Decide where speed and convenience shortcuts (mixes, room-temp skips, one-bowl) are acceptable versus where they degrade crumb quality.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Some shortcuts save time with negligible crumb cost

cons.claim: Skipping room-temp emulsification breaks batter and coarsens crumb

revisit_triggers: quality drop traced to a shortcut

nodes.definition: Scale a validated baker's-percentage formula to a target yield and pan/liner size while preserving ratios and bake behavior.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Percentage formulas scale exactly without re-tuning ratios

cons.claim: Scaling by eye drifts ratios and changes the crumb
cons.example: rounded cups change fill and bake time

nodes.definition: Use acidic dairy (buttermilk, sour cream) to tenderize via pH, react with soda for lift, and add moisture and tang without breaking balance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bake test outcome or ratio revision changes structure/tenderness balance

pros.claim: Buttermilk tenderizes by pH and activates soda for a soft, tangy crumb
pros.example: sour cream adds moisture and richness

cons.claim: Unbalanced acid leaves excess soda or curdles dairy
cons.example: too much acid without soda tastes sour

failure_modes: ignoring dairy fat in fat budget
acceptance_tests: dairy fat counted in fat budget

lever budgeting reads each ingredient as a percentage
edges.example: fat at 50% is a tenderizer dose

edges.why_related: hydration is flour:liquid percentage
flour is the primary structure lever
edges.benefit_of_coupling: flour choice grounded in lever model

edges.why_related: egg is a structure-building lever
edges.risk_of_conflict: egg set blind to structure need

edges.why_related: sugar is the primary tenderizing lever
fat is a tenderizing lever
leavening tenderizes by opening structure
method controls gluten from the chosen flour
fat state dictates mixing approach

structure holds the risen dome

flavor balance starts from sugar load

edges.why_related: component flavor feeds assembled balance
egg presence drives doneness safety
method choice frames shortcut tradeoffs

dairy acid activates soda

edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the moistness vs structure tension
edges.resolution_rule: structure budget dominates once collapse risk appears; cap sugar or add egg/flour to restore set

edges.why_related: more fat tenderizes but suppresses rise and dome
edges.resolution_rule: if dome target fails, rise dominates; reduce fat or add structure before chasing tenderness

edges.why_related: over-leavening lifts then collapses structure
edges.resolution_rule: structure dominates past collapse threshold; cut leavening to what structure can hold

edges.why_related: raising sugar for moisture flattens flavor complexity
edges.resolution_rule: balance with salt/acid first; only raise sugar for moisture when flavor contrast preserved

edges.why_related: speed shortcuts conflict with crumb quality
edges.resolution_rule: quality dominates on emulsification-critical steps; allow shortcuts only where crumb impact is negligible

edges.why_related: fresh-texture optimization conflicts with shelf-life moisture
edges.resolution_rule: weight by intended hold time; if multi-day, shelf-life levers dominate fresh-only tuning

edges.why_related: component sweetness conflicts with assembled balance
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names cake vs frosting sweetness tension
edges.resolution_rule: assembled budget dominates; lower cake sugar when frosting is very sweet

edges.why_related: moistness/underbake for keeping conflicts with safe doneness
edges.resolution_rule: food safety strictly dominates; never underbake for moistness, achieve moisture via formula instead

edges.why_related: texture-driven choices conflict with safety limits
edges.resolution_rule: food safety strictly dominates all crumb levers; allergen and doneness limits are non-negotiable

edges.why_related: high-ratio rule bounds maximum sugar load
edges.resolution_rule: if sugar exceeds liquid-carrying capacity, raise liquid or cap sugar to hold emulsion

edges.why_related: high-ratio balance bounds fat load
edges.resolution_rule: if fat destabilizes batter, reduce fat or rebalance liquid/egg to preserve emulsion

edges.why_related: bake-through requirement bounds underbaking for shape
edges.resolution_rule: doneness floor dominates; adjust temp/time for full bake even if dome shape suffers

conflict_axes.trigger: raising sugar/fat/liquid for moistness weakens the crumb's ability to hold shape
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if collapse risk appears, structure side dominates and tenderizers are capped
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: visible sinking or wet streak in trial bake
conflict_axes.example: high-sugar high-oil batter sinks without enough egg

conflict_axes.trigger: more tenderizer softens structure that rise depends on, flattening the dome
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if dome target fails, rise side dominates and fat/sugar are reduced
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: flat or sunken tops in trial
conflict_axes.example: excess fat gives flat dense cupcakes

conflict_axes.trigger: raising sugar for moisture and sweetness flattens perceived flavor complexity
resolution_order: raise sugar only if contrast preserved
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: flavor balance dominates until salt/acid contrast is in place

conflict_axes.trigger: optimizing cake sweetness alone makes the frosted product cloying
resolution_order: split sugar between cake and frosting
conflict_axes.example: sweet cake under sweet buttercream overwhelms

conflict_axes.trigger: speed shortcuts degrade emulsification and crumb quality
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: crumb quality drop traced to a shortcut

conflict_axes.trigger: tuning for peak fresh texture leaves cupcakes stale within a day
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if multi-day hold required, shelf-life dominates fresh-only tuning
conflict_axes.example: lean formula tastes great fresh, stale next day

conflict_axes.trigger: underbaking or raw-ingredient choices for texture create a safety hazard
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: food safety strictly dominates all texture and shelf-life levers

conflict_axes.trigger: pushing sugar past the liquid's carrying capacity breaks the high-ratio emulsion
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: emulsion stability dominates; sugar is bounded by liquid capacity
conflict_axes.example: sugar above liquid weight curdles batter

conflict_axes.trigger: developing gluten for structure can overshoot into toughness against tenderness goals
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if crumb is tough, tenderness side dominates and gluten development is reduced
conflict_axes.example: overmixed AP flour makes chewy cupcakes

edge_cases.trigger: cold ingredients or excess fat break the batter emulsion
edge_cases.failure_mode: curdled batter bakes greasy and coarse
edge_cases.example: butter at fridge temperature curdles the mix
edge_cases.detection_method: visual batter curdle check before scaling

edge_cases.failure_mode: grainy undissolved sugar and weak set
edge_cases.example: sugar above liquid weight stays gritty

edge_cases.failure_mode: over-rise then collapse with coarse crumb
edge_cases.example: double the powder sinks the center

edge_cases.trigger: underbaking to keep the center moist
resolution: achieve moisture via formula not underbake

edge_cases.trigger: cutting sugar for less sweetness without offsetting moisture
edge_cases.example: low-sugar cupcakes dry by next day

edge_cases.trigger: high-protein flour used for tender cake

edge_cases.failure_mode: soapy taste and dark uneven color
resolution: add acid or switch to baking powder

edge_cases.trigger: scaling by eye instead of percentage
edge_cases.failure_mode: ratio drift changes crumb at volume

edge_cases.trigger: sweet cake paired with sweet frosting

edge_cases.detection_method: allergen audit of ingredients and line

edge_cases.example: too much oil leaves an oily crumb

workflow.objective: express all ingredients as baker's percentages on a flour base
workflow.do_first_because: all ratio decisions depend on a stable base

workflow.objective: enforce sugar>=flour, liquid>=sugar, and full hydration for a stable emulsion
workflow.do_first_because: emulsion stability bounds all later levers

workflow.objective: classify ingredients as structure-builders or tenderizers and set a crumb target
acceptance_tests: each ingredient labeled toughener or tenderizer
workflow.do_first_because: lever map guides every ingredient choice

workflow.objective: set flour protein, egg, and mixing method to hit the structure budget
workflow.do_first_because: structure must be set before tenderizers push against it

workflow.objective: set sugar, fat, and acidic dairy for tenderness, moisture, and flavor
set leavening and bake profile for target rise, dome, and color
workflow.do_first_because: rise and bake settings determine final structure set

workflow.objective: verify doneness, raw-ingredient safety, and allergen control
workflow.do_first_because: safety gates release before any consumer tasting

workflow.objective: score crumb and shelf-life against target and map defects to levers
balance sweetness, flavor complexity, and coordination with frosting
workflow.do_first_because: flavor balance finalizes the eating experience

workflow.objective: scale the validated formula to yield and decide acceptable shortcuts
workflow.do_first_because: locking happens after all balance and safety gates pass

dominance_rules.trigger: texture or shelf-life choice conflicts with food safety
dominance_rules.rule: food safety overrides all flavor and texture decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: enforce doneness and allergen limits before any tasting
dominance_rules.example: never underbake for a moister center

dominance_rules.rule: structure floor dominates when collapse risk appears

dominance_rules.trigger: sugar load exceeds liquid carrying capacity
dominance_rules.example: liquid must meet or exceed sugar weight

dominance_rules.trigger: dome target fails due to excess tenderizer
dominance_rules.rule: rise target dominates when dome is the goal

dominance_rules.trigger: component sweetness conflicts with assembled balance
dominance_rules.rule: assembled-product sweetness budget dominates component optimization
dominance_rules.required_action: lower cake sugar when frosting is very sweet

dominance_rules.trigger: multi-day hold required but formula tuned for fresh-only
dominance_rules.rule: shelf-life dominates fresh-only tuning when hold time is multi-day

dominance_rules.trigger: speed shortcut hits an emulsification-critical step
dominance_rules.rule: crumb quality dominates on emulsification-critical steps

dominance_rules.trigger: flavor reads one-note from excess sugar
dominance_rules.rule: flavor balance dominates until salt/acid contrast is in place
override_requires: moisture target unmet by other means

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the baker's-percentage base before any ratio work
anti_rework_rules.rationale: all ratios depend on a stable flour base
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: ratios set without a defined base
anti_rework_rules.example: picking sugar load before flour base

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate high-ratio balance before tuning individual levers
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: levers tuned on an unstable batter

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the structure budget before choosing tenderizers
anti_rework_rules.rationale: tenderizers must push against a known structure floor
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tenderizers set with no structure budget
anti_rework_rules.example: adding fat with no structure plan

anti_rework_rules.rule: lock structure design before leavening and bake profile
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rise depends on the structure it lifts

anti_rework_rules.rule: clear the food-safety gate before consumer tasting or sale
anti_rework_rules.rationale: safety is non-negotiable and overrides texture

anti_rework_rules.rule: evaluate crumb against a rubric before iterating levers
coordinate cake and frosting sweetness before locking sugar
anti_rework_rules.rationale: assembled balance can change cake sugar
anti_rework_rules.example: finalizing sweet cake under sweet frosting

anti_rework_rules.rule: scale only from validated baker's percentages
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: scaling a non-finalized formula by guess

iteration_protocol.trigger: crumb too dry or too tough
batter curdles or sugar stays grainy
stale or dry by intended hold day
assembled product judged cloying or one-note
